text:
jon_customer: Hey team — started ~09:10 UTC our production app saw a burst of 502s and much higher latency. Noticed a few 401s too. Our dashboards show traffic routed to eu-west even though we pin us-west. Billing spike as well. Any idea why failover happened?

sam_support: Sorry — that sounds bad. Can you paste an example request/response (curl + x-request-id) and any headers you set? Also were you using short-lived tokens?

jon_customer: Example curl we used: 
```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-xxxx" -H "X-Client-Region: us-west" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```
Response we got for one failed attempt: 
```
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
x-request-id: req_ABC123
x-region: eu-west-1
{"error":"upstream timeout"}
```
And occasionally a 401 payload: `{"error":"invalid_token","message":"token issued in us-west but validated in eu-west"}`

sam_support: Thanks, escalating to SRE. @elaine_sre can you pull healthcheck + routing logs for req_ABC123 and the 09:08-09:15 window?

elaine_sre: On it. Quick read shows the healthcheck agent marked the us-west pool UNHEALTHY at 2026-03-17T09:10:02Z due to probe auth failures, then orchestrator triggered auto-failover to eu-west at 09:11:05Z for org-452. Probe debug snippet: 
```text
[09:09:58] probe ping to us-west-control timed out
[09:10:01] probe auth error: 403 from firewall (source IP 34.200.21.45)
[09:11:05] orchestrator: promoting eu-west pool for customer org-452 (auto-failover)
```
That 403 looks like the probe was blocked, so this is a likely false-negative health.

maria_network: That source IP (34.200.21.45) matches the NAT egress pool we rotated during a maintenance window at 09:09. We didn't realize probes relied on a fixed allowlist. NAT rotation + an ACL expecting old IPs = probe rejected. Also saw short BGP path flaps returning some traffic to eu-west for ~30s.

ops-bot: incident events: 
- 2026-03-17T09:09:40Z probe-maintenance-start (network)
- 2026-03-17T09:10:02Z healthcheck: us-west status=unhealthy -> reason=probe403
- 2026-03-17T09:11:05Z routing-controller: failover us-west->eu-west for org-452
- 2026-03-17T09:13:20Z billing: cross-region-eval increment for org-452

billing_bot: org-452 shows an egress / cross-region billing bump during the window. Also the 401s likely from token validation hitting a different region's auth cluster — short-lived tokens validated against issuer bound to us-west failed when routed to eu-west. We'll draft refund estimate.

sam_support: Repro steps: @jon_customer can you try forcing region header to confirm it stays in us-west? Also please paste the x-request-id for a recent failure if available.

jon_customer: I retried with header `X-Force-Region: us-west` and the same request succeeded immediately. New request id `req_DEF456`. So forcing region kept us in us-west.

elaine_sre: Preliminary mitigation plan: 
1) Add current NAT pool ranges to probe allowlist asap.
2) Pause automatic cross-region failover when healthcheck reason == probe-auth (403) AND a maintenance flag exists for network ops (to avoid false-negatives).
3) Add a 30s canary/verification delay for orgs with billing-sensitive tags before switching region.
I'll open an incident ticket and PR for the routing-controller changes.

maria_network: We'll also: 
- coordinate to avoid NAT pool rotations during probe windows,
- add probe auth via ephemeral signed certs (less reliant on source IP allowlist),
- review BGP announcement timing to minimize short flaps.

billing_bot: I'll compute a provisional refund and list customers affected. Recommend temporarily disabling auto-billing for cross-region surge while we run the postmortem.

sam_support: Actions assigned: @billing_bot refund estimate, @elaine_sre incident + PR, @maria_network NAT rotation controls, I'll follow up with @jon_customer about the refund and status. Sorry for the disruption :disappointed:.

jon_customer: Thanks — appreciate the fast triage. Please CC me on the incident ticket and the PR so we can track. :thumbsup:
